1.explanation:
• src/ol/source/DataTile.js – this source creates the tile canvas or typed-array at the custom tileSizes; if the downstream upload logic mis-reads its row length or stride, the upload will be truncated or padded.

• src/ol/tilegrid/TileGrid.js – stores the tileSizes_ array ([770,768], [240,240], …) and provides the size information used throughout the renderer and texture code. Any mis-indexing here would propagate wrong dimensions to the texture upload.

• src/ol/webgl/TileTexture.js – central class that creates WebGL textures (gl.createTexture), sets UNPACK parameters (UNPACK_ALIGNMENT, UNPACK_ROW_LENGTH, UNPACK_SKIP_PIXELS, etc.) and calls texImage2D/texSubImage2D. The warning stems from a mismatch in the width/height it passes versus the buffer’s actual shape.

• src/ol/renderer/webgl/TileLayer.js – orchestrates fetching tiles from DataTile, passing them to TileTexture, and drawing them. It computes the tile’s zoom level, resolution and may choose between fullImage vs subImage uploads; a logic bug here could lead to wrong offsets or sizes.

• src/ol/layer/WebGLTile.js – defines the high-level layer interface and ties into the WebGL renderer. It passes layer styles/shaders and may influence how texture coordinates or padding are applied.

Together these files form the end-to-end path from DataTile’s raw pixel buffer, through the tile grid’s custom dimensions, into the WebGL texture upload that is currently being given the wrong dimensions (hence the "desired upload requires more data than available" warning). A fix will live in the TileTexture upload logic and possibly how TileLayer/WebGLTile invoke it, with awareness of non-standard tileSizes from TileGrid/DataTile.
1.bug_scenario:
A user is loading non-power-of-two tiles (770×768 at zoom 0, then 240×240 at higher zooms) via an ol.source.DataTile with a custom tile grid (extent [0,–23828,23903,0], sizes [[1,1],[7,7],[25,25],[100,100]], tileSizes [[770,768],[240,240],[240,240],[240,240]]). When they render that source with an ol.layer.WebGLTile/WebGLTileLayer, the tiles show up completely black and the console logs a WebGL warning:

“texImage: Desired upload requires more data than is available: (767 rows plus 770 pixels needed, 767 rows plus 258 pixels available)”

That message indicates a mismatch between the width/height the WebGL code is trying to upload and the actual pixel data buffer. Prior to PRs 11532 or 12024 this did not occur, so the bug is almost certainly in the parts of the WebGL pipeline that compute texture sizes, set up gl.pixelStore parameters and call gl.texImage2D/subImage2D when given arbitrary tile sizes.

2.explanation:
• src/ol/source/DataTile.js
  – Calculates the canvas width/height for each tile from the custom TileGrid. An off-by-one or partial‐tile case here propagates an unexpected image size to WebGL.

• src/ol/tilegrid/TileGrid.js
  – Stores and returns the tileSizes_ array. Any flaw in how the custom tileSizes are normalized or interpreted will feed wrong dimensions into both DataTile and the WebGLTile renderer.

• src/ol/layer/WebGLTile.js
  – The layer entry point that wires the DataTile source into the WebGLTile renderer. If it assumes power-of-two textures or ignores partial‐tile logic from DataTile, it will configure the renderer incorrectly.

• src/ol/renderer/webgl/TileLayer.js
  – Builds the draw lists, binds tile canvases to textures, and calls the TileTexture helper. A mismatch between the tile’s reported width/height and the renderer’s expectations leads straight to the texImage failure.

• src/ol/webgl/TileTexture.js
  – Low-level code that calls gl.texImage2D/gl.texSubImage2D. It currently computes the upload width/height (and any padding to power-of-two) incorrectly for nonstandard tile sizes, so the byte length of the supplied ArrayBufferView doesn’t cover the full texture area requested.

Fixing this bug will involve aligning how DataTile (and TileGrid) report the true pixel dimensions of each tile with how the WebGL TileLayer and TileTexture consume those dimensions when allocating and uploading GPU textures.
2.bug_scenario:
When using an ol.layer.WebGLTile together with an ol.source.DataTile and a completely custom TileGrid (extent [0, –23828, 23903, 0] and tile sizes [[770,768], [240,240], …]), the WebGLTile layer comes back completely black and emits this console warning:

  WebGL warning: texImage: Desired upload requires more data than is available: (767 rows plus 770 pixels needed, 767 rows plus 258 pixels available)

In other words, the dimensions that DataTile computes for its off-screen canvas no longer match the width/height (or the padded power-of-two texture size) that the WebGLTile renderer and its TileTexture helper use when calling gl.texImage2D. The mismatch in stride/rows causes WebGL to abort the upload and you end up with blank tiles.
